With just weeks to go until the midterm elections, President Trump continues to campaign for Republican candidates in GOP-friendly states. Today he's in Tennessee.
Last night he was in central New York, where his rally drew demonstrations. Bryson Pace with member station WAER has more.
Protesters gathered by the thousands in downtown Syracuse, as President Donald Trump campaigned for Republicans a few blocks away.
Mayor Sharon Owens spoke on behalf of Syracuse, a city the U.S. Census Bureau ranks fourth in the nation for child poverty.
I don't agree with removing SNAP benefits from people who need food security. I don't agree with the methods for immigration reform.
I believe that there is a process that needs to be improved, but the way it's going now is not protecting us, it's harming us.
A portion of the crowd peeled away to confront Trump supporters.
They were met by a barricade of police officers and quickly faded.
For NPR News, I'm Bryson Pace in Syracuse, New York.
Opponents of capital punishment are marking today as World Day Against the Death Penalty.
In Pierce-Jason DeRose reports, this comes as the U.S. grapples with two high-profile death penalty cases.
The botched lethal injection of Christa Pike in Tennessee and the announced livestreaming of the firing squad execution of Fort Hood shooter Nadel Hassan has put the issue at the forefront of people's minds.
World Day Against the Death Penalty was created in 2003 to draw attention to what advocates call an unjust practice.
The day draws support from both secular human rights activists and many people of faith who oppose capital punishment.
The United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights issued a statement this week criticizing the death penalty as often falling short of international human rights standards.
The U.N. says more than 25,000 people worldwide were on death row last year and more than 2,700 people were executed.
Jason DeRose, NPR News.
And you're listening to NPR News from Washington.
Russian strikes have killed at least 15 people, including three children.
This a day after President Trump announced a deal to buy Russian diesel, a move Kiev warned could fund Moscow's war efforts.
Ukraine is struggling to counter escalating Russian attacks, which have killed over 60 people in the past four days.
Ukraine's President Zelensky criticized the diesel deal, saying it plays into Russia's hands and could prolong the conflict.
Anger and resignation are growing in Kiev over the situation.
Gas prices around the world have soared after the U.S. started the war in Iran in February.
AAA says the cost of a gallon of regular is $4.36 today.
A new study has found that American shoppers will feel some sticker shock as they stock up on Halloween candy this year.
NPR's John Stoleness reports it's a continuing trend.
This is no trick.
The average price of a 100-piece bag of assorted candy is almost $17 this year.
That's up 3.5 percent from last Halloween.
It continues.
A five-year trend that has seen the cost of bags of Halloween candy increase by 71 percent, a little over $7 a bag.
The study by FinanceBuzz analyzed the prices of bulk Halloween sweets at four major supermarkets, Walmart, Target, Kroger and Albertsons.
Analysts blame a rising price of cocoa due to environmental factors and supply problems in Ghana and the Ivory Coast.
Total consumer spending on Halloween is expected to reach $13.5 billion this year.
John Stoleness, NPR News.
And I'm Janine Herbst, NPR News in Washington.
